alternative_explanations: The learner may only extract a finite transition dictionary from differences, while all apparent semantic composition is ordinary table reuse or symbolic anti-unification.
Sparse event execution may be exactly Rete matching or a pointer state machine, leaving no computational distinction for ACC/SCCS.
A dense full-sweep baseline may overstate the benefit because optimized sparse tensors or change masks can skip dormant nodes without adopting chemical semantics.
confounds: Particle slots, directed adjacency, active flags and a finite four-symbol alphabet are supplied by the benchmark; they are a strong hand-written ontology and prevent broad semantic claims.
Every fresh query and update is provided as a dense K-particle state, so locating the event incurs K-dependent parsing; a delta-stream interface would remove this cost for both ACC/SCCS and Rete.
falsification_criteria: Reduce HYP-0003 if learned_semantic_reactor has exact or held-out accuracy below 0.95 in any cell, fails any observed local rule, does not converge, oscillates, activates more than D events, or fails the registered operation advantage over the full sweep at K=32 and D=4/6.

Treat the separate ACC/SCCS thesis as null and stop tuning if rete_reaction_engine or learned_reaction_recurrent matches semantic-reactor capability while being no worse on exact operations, bytes, state and continual-update work; a new name for a production system is not a positive result.

outcome_policy.negative: If the semantic reactor fails unseen composition, convergence or sparse activation, lower HYP-0003 toward dormant and do not patch the toy chemistry.
outcome_policy.null: If learned reactions compose exactly but Rete or pointer recurrence matches or dominates them, lower HYP-0003, preserve the mechanism as a production-system control and pivot to a different family.
outcome_policy.positive: Only a capability-exact, non-dominated learned reactor with a distinction beyond Rete and pointer recurrence may remain testing and earn an adversarial multi-seed screen; no quick result can be called promising.

predicted_outcome: Training contains fifteen deterministic local rule instances as unlabeled dense before/after particle states and withholds one rule for a continual-update check. Every scored target is an unseen D-step composition whose full transition is absent from training. Random and whole-trajectory memorizer exact accuracy are at most 0.125. Learned sweep, pointer recurrent, Rete, semantic reactor and oracle reach exact held-out accuracy at least 0.95 in every cell, observed-rule accuracy 1, convergence 1 and oscillation 0. The semantic reactor activates exactly D events, scans dense input once, uses fewer than half the query operations of learned full sweep at K=32 and D=4/6, but has a positive full-system K slope and update work growing with K. Rete or pointer recurrent is expected to match or improve its accuracy, operations, state and update signature, yielding a preregistered null for a distinct ACC/SCCS architecture.
promotion_criteria: Quick cannot promote HYP-0003. A later screen is justified only if the learned semantic reactor passes every capability gate, is non-dominated by Rete, recurrent, sweep and oracle controls on exact accounting, shows a reusable learned-rule or local-update signature not supplied by object slots and event pointers, and acknowledges SRC-0030 through SRC-0034.
research_question: Can a persistent event-driven substrate infer reusable local reaction rules from unlabeled full-state transitions, compose them on unseen particle graphs, and retain a distinct end-to-end cost or update signature beyond conventional Rete matching and a pointer recurrent controller?
title: Unlabeled semantic reaction composition versus Rete and recurrent controls
